results.title: CheckinBee Review 2026: $13/mo Text Check-Ins, No App Needed | CheckRise
results.content:
1. Website issues. Multiple pages on the CheckinBee site have shown problems, including links that redirect elsewhere and pages that do not load as expected. For a service you are trusting with a daily safety routine, a shaky website is a yellow flag worth taking seriously.

2. Stale content. The CheckinBee blog and public content have not been meaningfully updated in a long time. As with any safety service, limited visible activity makes it harder to judge how actively the product is being developed and supported.

3. No voice call escalation. When a check-in is missed, CheckinBee notifies your contacts. It does not place an automated phone call to the person or to your contacts, so the alert still depends on someone seeing a notification.

Test it end to end before you rely on it [...] No commitment. Cancel anytime.

## The Bottom Line

CheckinBee has the right idea: text-based daily check-ins with no app, at a low entry price, from a BBB-accredited company. The hesitation is execution. Reported website issues, stale content, and notification-only escalation mean you should test it thoroughly before trusting it with someone who lives alone.

If it tests clean and you only need one daily check-in, it is a budget option. If you want the same SMS convenience with real escalation and multiple check-ins included, compare it against an actively maintained alternative first. The point of a check-in service is that the alert never quietly fails, so make sure whichever you pick actually delivers it.
